advantages.what: Refuses an assignment body with an invalid UTF-8 byte instead of storing a replacement character that becomes the notice recipient
CLI quotes names and prints 'unassigned', so an agent named '-' or 'null' cannot be mistaken for an unassigned ticket
Decision record 0009 for the format and notice-key choices
CHANGELOG 1.5.0 section and package.json bumped to 1.5.0; Z has only an Unreleased section and no version bump
Failed save rolled back and answered 500 for PATCH, transition and assignment; Z does this for assignment only
Documents where the assignment notice goes (agent name as given, no address lookup)

Lighter to carry: Z hand-parses the assignee filter, spreads strict UTF-8 rules over three files, ships acceptance/ and working notes in the tree, and its 24 tests are pinned to exact strings, sequence numbers and internals
Keeps the existing first-value rule for a repeated status/priority parameter; Y changed it so different values list nothing

pairs.why: Both deliver every stated requirement and handle the unsaid conditions soundly. Z's edge is two low defects (D-1, D-3); Y's is the release record (D-2), wider save rollback and a lighter codebase and test suite to keep. These offset each other, and each side's gaps are small.
